explanation: Compared against OEIS A262781 (Zhi-Wei Sun): a(n) is the number of ways to write n = x² + φ(y²) + φ(z²) with x ≥ 0, 0 < y ≤ z and y or z prime; 'Conjecture: (i) a(n) > 0 for all n > 6'. In Lean a n counts triples with x ≤ n, 1 ≤ y ≤ z ≤ n satisfying the condition; the bounds lose nothing since φ(y²) = y·φ(y) ≥ y. Tests match the data (0, 0, 1, 2, 1). The statement 0 < a n for n > 6 is the conjecture. Faithful.
